news.title: The Army Just Did Something Extraordinary To Break China’s Rare Earth Monopoly
news.summary: On November 3, the Pentagon did something it’s never done before. The Army signed a non-binding term sheet to host a commercial rare earth plant on one of its own bases, under a lease that could run past the year 2100. And the company it chose, REalloys (NASDAQ: ALOY), already has a head start on what the Army needs most: turning rare earths into metal outside of China. analysis.summary: The U.S. Army signed a non-binding term sheet to host a commercial rare earth processing plant at Utah's Tooele Army Depot.
analysis.rationale: The item concerns domestic rare earth supply chains and defense infrastructure rather than crude oil production, refining, or demand.

news.title: Why Iraq Just Fast-Tracked Chevron’s Takeover Of A 14-Billion-Barrel Supergiant

analysis.summary: Chevron and Iraq finalized commercial terms for the supergiant West Qurna 2 oilfield ahead of the February 2027 exclusivity deadline.

news.title: Airlines Face Fuel Crisis as Price Hedges Expire
news.summary: Reports about an oil glut are back in the media, and U.S. diesel just dropped below $6 per gallon. But these signs of normalization have yet to reach the airline industry, where jet fuel prices remain eye-wateringly high and hedging contracts are expiring. It seems not all airlines will survive the winter. Airlines have been among the sectors to feel the most immediate pain from the fallout of the war between the United States and Israel, and Iran. With jet fuel representing a solid portion of the industry’s expenses, the fuel price jump…

analysis.summary: Airlines face expiring fuel hedges and elevated jet fuel costs from the U.S.-Israel-Iran war even as oil glut reports and lower diesel prices emerge.
analysis.rationale: The text cites both bearish supply-glut signals and falling diesel alongside bullish war-driven jet fuel tightness and potential airline demand destruction.

news.title: Uganda Pushes First Oil to Mid-2027 as Iran War Holds Up Equipment
news.summary: Uganda’s dream to achieve its first commercial oil production and crude exports has been delayed yet again, extending the country’s wait to more than two decades since commercial oil reserves were first discovered in the country in 2006. Officials from the Uganda National Oil Company (UNOC) and the Petroleum Authority of Uganda (PAU) have announced that Uganda’s first oil production and exports have now been pushed back to before the end of June 2027, blaming the delay on international supply chain bottlenecks and disruptions…

analysis.summary: Uganda delayed its first commercial oil production and exports to mid-2027 due to supply chain bottlenecks linked to the Iran war.
analysis.rationale: Pushing back new crude export capacity removes expected future supply from the market, though Uganda's output has been repeatedly delayed.

news.title: Can Underwater Data Centers Escape the Land-Based Backlash?
news.summary: The AI boom is pushing developers to test a new frontier for positioning data centers, following the growing backlash against the excessive use of land, water, and energy resources onshore. So hyperscalers and start-ups have moved to test placing data centers under the sea or floating on ships, to save on water, land, and electricity use. Data centers in the ocean could significantly reduce freshwater and power use for cooling and could source electricity from offshore wind farms or tidal wave power projects, reducing concerns among communities…

analysis.summary: Hyperscalers and start-ups are testing underwater and ship-based data centers powered by offshore wind or tidal energy.
analysis.rationale: The story focuses on AI data center siting, water use, and offshore renewable electricity with no direct implication for crude oil prices.

news.title: China’s Coal Power Generation Slumps as Wind and Solar Surge
news.summary: China’s thermal power generation fell from a year earlier for the fourth consecutive month in October, with year-to-date thermal power output down by 0.1%, according to official data compiled by Bloomberg. analysis.rationale: The shift primarily displaces coal in China's power sector rather than crude oil used in transport and petrochemicals.
